'''Chandra Kumar Naranbhai Patel''' (born 2 July 1938) is an Indian-American [[electrical engineer]]. He is best known for developing the [[carbon dioxide laser]] in 1963, now widely used in industrial cutting and [[dermatology]].<ref>{{cite journal |author=Patel, C. K. N. |year=1964 |title=Continuous-Wave Laser Action on Vibrational-Rotational Transitions of CO<sub>2</sub> |journal=Physical Review |volume=136 |issue=5A |pages=A1187–A1193 |bibcode=1964PhRv..136.1187P |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.136.A1187 |doi-access=free}}</ref>

Patel was born in [[Baramati]], [[India]], and received a [[Bachelor of Engineering]] (B.E.) degree from the [[College of Engineering, Pune|Government College of Engineering, Pune]] and an M.S. and PhD in [[electrical engineering]] from [[Stanford University]] in 1959 and 1961.<ref>{{cite web|title=C. Kumar N. Patel|url=https://www.aip.org/history-programs/niels-bohr-library/oral-histories/31404|publisher=The American Institute of Physics|access-date=7 September 2019|date=27 March 2015}}</ref> Patel joined [[Bell Laboratories]] the same year and subsequently became Executive Director of the Research, Materials Science, Engineering and Academic Affairs Division at AT&T Bell Laboratories in [[Murray Hill, New Jersey]]. Patel's discovery of the laser action in 1963 on the [[Rotational–vibrational coupling|rotational–vibrational transitions]] of [[carbon dioxide]] and his discovery in 1964 of efficient vibrational energy transfer between [[molecule]]s, led to a series of experiments which demonstrated that the carbon dioxide laser was capable of very high [[continuous-wave]] and pulsed [[Power (physics)|power]] output at very high conversion efficiencies. From 1993–1999, Patel served as vice chancellor for research at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]], where he is also a [[Emeritus|Professor Emeritus]] of physics and electrical engineering.<ref name="NSF">{{cite web|url=https://www.nsf.gov/od/nms/recip_details.cfm?recip_id=270|title=The President's National Medal of Science: Recipient Details|access-date=7 September 2019|publisher=The National Science Foundation}}</ref>

[[File:C. Kumar Patel - National Medal of Science, 1996.webm|thumb|Patel discussing his career and his invention of the carbon dioxide laser.]]
In 1996, [[Bill Clinton|President Bill Clinton]] awarded Patel the [[National Medal of Science]], "for his fundamental contributions to quantum electronics and invention of the carbon dioxide laser, which have had significant impact on industrial, scientific, medical, and defense applications."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nationalmedals.org/laureates/c-kumar-n-patel#|title=C. Kumar N. Patel|access-date=7 September 2019}}</ref> In addition to the carbon dioxide laser, he also developed the "spin-flip" infrared [[Raman laser]] and was inducted into the [[National Inventors Hall of Fame|National Inventors Hall of Fame (NIHF)]] in 2012.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://lemelson.mit.edu/resources/kumar-patel|title=MIT Inventor of the Week: Kumar Patel|work=The Lemelson-MIT Program|access-date=7 September 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-01-18 |title=NIHF Inductee C. Kumar N. Patel Invented the Carbon Dioxide (CO2) Laser |url=https://www.invent.org/inductees/c-kumar-n-patel |access-date=2026-01-18 |website=www.invent.org |language=en}}</ref>

Patel currently holds 36 U.S. [[patent]]s relating to lasers and [[laser applications]]. He is a member of the [[National Academy of Engineering]] and the [[National Academy of Sciences]], and a Fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ucla.edu/about/awards-and-honors/faculty/american-academy-of-arts-and-sciences|title=UCLA Members of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences|publisher=UCLA|access-date=7 September 2019}}</ref> the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aaas.org/sites/default/files/AnnualReports/2008/aaas_ann_rpt_08k_fellows.pdf|title=AAAS Fellows|access-date=7 September 2019}}</ref> the [[American Physical Society]], the [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers|IEEE]], the [[The Optical Society|Optical Society of America]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.osa.org/en-us/history/biographies/bios/c_kumar_n_patel/|title=C. Kumar N. Patel|publisher=The Optical Society|access-date=7 September 2019}}</ref> the [[Laser Institute of America]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lia.org/about-lia/awards-nominations/fellow-award|title=Fellow Award|publisher=Laser Institute of America|access-date=7 September 2019|date=8 May 2017}}{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> the American Society of Laser Medicine, and a Senior Fellow of the [[California Council on Science and Technology]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ccst.us/people/senior-fellows/c-kumar-n-patel/|title=C. Kumar N. Patel|publisher=CCST|access-date=7 September 2019}}</ref>

In 2018 C. Kumar N. Patel became an Honorary Member of the American Laser Study Club<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.indiawest.com/news/global_indian/american-laser-study-club-names-c-kumar-n-patel-as/article_0b47470e-6388-11e8-90f1-776bda0c6811.html|title=American Laser Study Club Names C. Kumar N. Patel as Honorary Member|work=India West|date=30 May 2018|access-date=7 September 2019|archive-date=3 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180903010913/http://www.indiawest.com/news/global_indian/american-laser-study-club-names-c-kumar-n-patel-as/article_0b47470e-6388-11e8-90f1-776bda0c6811.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> which a year later named an award in his honor.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.americanlaserstudyclub.org/annual-award/|title=Kumar Patel Prize|publisher=American Laser Study Club|access-date=7 September 2019}}</ref>

*[[Charles Hard Townes Medal]] (1982)
